main_text.l: Patriarchæ, Job, Moses, David, Prophetæ & Apostoli & alii,
omnes perseverantiæ donô insignes fuerint, & tamen nul-
lus eorum pietati renuncia vit aut inimicus fuit; Si hæc do-
ctrina de Perseverantia trahitur ad lasciviam carnis, teste
Juda v. 4. fit hoc per accidens; Hæc autem præcipua illo-
rum hypothesis, quâ docent certitudinem perseverantiæ
stare non posse cum mediis hortationis, promissionum,
comminationum ex parte Dei, nec cum conditionibus vi-
gilantiæ, obedientiæ, precum ex parte nostra, eos fallit
& falluntur ex oppositione subordinatorum, nam finis in-
fallibilitas & certitudo non tollit, sed stabilit usum medio-
rum, & Sancti, qui per fidem norunt certam esse perseve-
rantiam, simul norunt absque sanctitate, fugâ peccati, ac
studio pietatis se eam assequi non posse, ideoque hæc pe-
tunt à Deo, & impetrant quoque, & sic per gratiam ipsius
perseverant: Illustratura simili, tum exemplis, Hiskiæ,
Esa.38. 5. 21. cui promissa vitæ prolongatio, & tamen ad-
hibitum emplastrum, tum Pauli Act. 27. 24. 31. qui certus
erat ex revelatione neminem periturum ex iis, qui
in navi erant, & tamen de nautis ait, si illi
discesserint, reliquos servari
non posse.
A MON-

page.notes: Woodcut ornament (flower vase) below the text, not transcribed. The catchword "A MON-" is printed at the lower right. Some words are set in italic (names of Scripture figures and "Prophetæ & Apostoli"). Certain words in the printed text are uncertain, such as "Illustratura" which reads as "Illustratura" with a macron-like mark; the printed line was "Illustratura" as read.
